messages:
anna: seeing p95/p99 spikes across multiple tenants starting ~10:40 UTC, lots of queued time before exec. customers reporting 5-20s tails.

support-bot: alert: ingress_queue_length > 500 for 5m (region: us-west-2).

mike: confirmed, node memory pressure in gke-us-west-2a; a handful of worker pods showing OOM restarts in the last 45m.

sean: quick grep of request logs shows a huge number of retries after 429s from auth-service => plausible retry storm into admission queue.

jen: note timeline — we rolled runtime rc-2.7 ~30m before the first spike. rc-2.7 changed batching/kvcache heuristics.

anna: can someone run a query for `admit_wait_ms` across tenants and group by tenant? need to see if this is tenant-local or global.

mike: query run against logs: most long-wait entries are tenant=acme-corp and tenant=platco, but there is non-zero tail in others too. median admit_wait_ms for acme is 2200ms, p99 =~ 15000ms.

jen: logs also show large input sizes from a small number of customers, causing longer per-request handling which increases queueing pressure. combined with retries it's a multiplier.

sean: repro steps if you want to reproduce locally: run the following from a test machine (concurrent 50 clients):

```bash
for i in {1..50}; do \
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer test-token" -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -d '{"input": "'$(head -c 32000 /dev/urandom | base64)'"}' &
done
wait
```

you'll see a bunch of `admit_wait_ms` spikes and some 429/503s depending on timing.

mike: short mitigation applied: scaled worker pool from 30 -> 60 in us-west-2 and bumped node pool autoscaling target. also kicked a rolling restart of affected runtime pods to clear leaked memory from rc-2.7.

deploy-bot: rollback: runtime-rc-2.7 -> runtime-rc-2.6 triggered by mike at 11:15 UTC.

anna: temporary config changes we made: 1) increase per-tenant soft concurrency for acme-corp and platco to 100, 2) lowered client retry window by returning 503 fast-fail for known retry loops, 3) enabled priority-routing to push small requests to a fast-path pool.

support-bot: sent proactive customer update to affected tenants: short note and ETA to stabilize.

sean: longer-term actions: 1) revert or patch rc-2.7 batching memory growth (probable cause), 2) add admission_control metrics per-tenant (queue depth, oldest-wait), 3) implement server-side retry-squelch for clients that hit repeated 429s, 4) tighten default client retry backoff in SDK.

jen: also propose a guard: if per-tenant queue depth > X and average request size > Y, automatically spin up a small dedicated fast-path pool to reduce tail amplification.

mike: I added an incident ticket (INC-1745) with runbook link and assigned eng-runtime + infra. runbook includes prometheus queries and the curl repro.

anna: assigning owners: eng-runtime -> jen, infra -> mike, support comms -> sean. please post updates here.

sean: one quick note — saw a batcher config in rc-2.7 that increased in-memory batch window to 200ms; that combined with large payloads explains memory pressure. patch incoming.

jen: patch PR opened (link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/332) to clamp batch window and lower max batch size for large-input routes.

mike: cluster scaled, rollback applied, runtimes restarted. early signs: ingress_queue_length back to normal, p95 down to 700ms for most tenants. monitoring will need a few more minutes.

anna: nice work. next: add per-tenant alert thresholds so we can page before p99 hits 10s. also add a short-term rule to reject very large single requests with a clearer 413 error to avoid queue amplification.

jen: ack, I'll have the 413 rule up as a feature flag for risky routes.

support-bot: incident note updated, customers notified that we rolled back runtime and scaled nodes.

anna: thanks all — staying on this until metrics are stable. :thumbsup:
